name: Power Products
description: You are given $$$n$$$ positive integers $$$a_1, \ldots, a_n$$$, and an integer $$$k \geq 2$$$. Count the number of pairs $$$i, j$$$ such that $$$1 \leq i \lt j \leq n$$$, and there exists an integer $$$x$$$ such that $$$a_i \cdot a_j = x^k$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$ ($$$2 \leq n \leq 10^5$$$, $$$2 \leq k \leq 100$$$). The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \leq a_i \leq 10^5$$$).
output_specification: Print a single integer — the number of suitable pairs.
approach_summary: Compute polynomial rolling hashes hash(s[0..i]) with prime base B and large modulo M. Check substring equality s[l1..r1] == s[l2..r2] in O(1) time.
